audit_findings.magnitude: filed $357.2 million enterprise fair value, $178.6 million purchase price, and $74.844 million net cash paid; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The acquisition changes the operating-earnings perimeter from a 50% equity-method interest to full consolidation, while the cash bridge already reflects acquisition funding.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, future financial results of Mattel163 will be consolidated and included in Mattel's consolidated financial statements subsequent to closing.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: FY2025 owner earnings represent the former equity-method structure, whereas the June 2026 bridge is post-acquisition. Mattel said pro-forma and actual results were not material for financial-statement disclosure, but that standard does not establish immateriality to this valuation. The acquisition's scale and Mattel163's reported contribution to 2026 growth and margins make it reasonably capable of changing estimated value, although the direction cannot be determined without consolidated cash earnings and reinvestment needs.
audit_findings.action: Re-run owner earnings on a consistent post-acquisition perimeter using full Mattel163 cash earnings, working capital, capital expenditures, acquisition-related costs, incremental amortization, taxes, and the cash consideration already reflected in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may include operating or inaccessible cash
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $523.856 million cash add-back, including $393.0 million held abroad and $75.5 million in Russia; computed maximum bridge exposure $1.71 per share or 10.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash that is required for seasonal operations, restricted, trapped, or costly to repatriate must be excluded from the non-operating cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Mattel intends to utilize its existing cash and cash equivalents, cash flow from operations, and borrowings under the Credit Facility to meet its short-term liquidity needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all June cash, while the filing identifies seasonal liquidity demands and limited transferability of Russian cash. The excess portion remains unresolved. Removing the full add-back as a bounding sensitivity lowers base value from $16.89 to approximately $15.18 per share, reducing the premium over the $14.53 market price from $2.36 to about $0.65; that is capable of changing the practical valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Determine unrestricted and repatriable cash by jurisdiction and calculate minimum liquidity after seasonal working-capital needs, acquisition obligations, taxes, and committed expenditures; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Unrecognized tax benefits are an omitted senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $168.9 million; computed $0.55 per share and 3.3% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Probable settlements not already captured in normalized cash taxes would reduce the equity bridge or future owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the unrecognized tax benefit balance, inclusive of interest and penalties, and net of U.S. federal tax benefit was $168.9 million and $151.7 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge contains no explicit reserve, but the amount and timing of any cash settlement remain unresolved and the accounting balance is not necessarily the eventual payment. Even a conservative full $168.9 million deduction would reduce base value only from $16.89 to about $16.34 per share, still above the $14.53 price, while leaving the bear/base/bull ordering unchanged. This concrete maximum-scale comparison does not support present materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the balance to the latest 10-Q, identify amounts already reflected in liabilities or normalized cash taxes, and rerun only for probable cash settlements not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a steady-state cost base
audit_findings.magnitude: filed FY2025 restructuring charges of $41.249 million and $53 million gap between $172 million realized and $225 million targeted annual gross savings; by June 2026, $18.376 million additional charges and a $20 million target gap remained
audit_findings.mechanism: Transitional restructuring costs and incomplete savings directly affect normalized owner earnings and the growth path applied to the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Targeted annual gross cost savings from actions associated with the OPG program, which are expected to be completed by the end of 2026, were increased from $200 million to $225 million in the fourth quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The transitional condition is demonstrated. FY2025 includes implementation charges while not containing the full targeted savings run-rate. The disclosed amounts are large relative to the $331.2 million owner-earnings anchor, but gross savings cannot be treated as net owner earnings because inflation, reinvestment, taxes, and execution shortfalls may offset them. The combined scale is reasonably capable of changing value, with direction mixed until a net steady-state bridge is established.
audit_findings.action: Bridge FY2025 owner earnings to a steady-state base using realized recurring savings only, subtract remaining cash implementation costs, inflation and required reinvestment, and rerun the scenarios without treating targeted gross savings as guaranteed earnings.

audit_findings.title: Recall and litigation costs may be a one-off retained in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $30.8 million FY2025 expense increase and $17.7 million lower related expense in first-half 2026; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A demonstrably nonrecurring cash cost could be normalized out of anchor owner earnings; recurring product-liability costs must remain in projected owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in other selling and administrative expenses was primarily due to higher expenses related to inclined sleeper product recalls and related litigation of $30.8 million and higher outside services and other expenses of $69.5 million, partially offset by lower employee compensation related expenses, including lower incentive compensation, of $50.2 million, and realized savings from the OPG program of $40.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $30.8 million expense in the anchor is demonstrated, but the record does not establish its cash incidence, insurance recovery, final settlement exposure, or nonrecurrence. Its stated amount is significant relative to the $331.2 million anchor, while the lower first-half 2026 expense suggests—but does not prove—normalization. The finding may affect value, but present evidence cannot establish either the proper adjustment or its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Trace the charge through recall reserves, operating cash flow, settlements and insurance recoveries; normalize only the after-tax cash portion proven nonrecurring and retain a recurring product-liability allowance before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: The anchor does not contain a full year of the new coupon burden
audit_findings.magnitude: computed $9.75 million annual pre-tax coupon increase; conservative dollar-for-dollar base-value sensitivity approximately $137 million or $0.45 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the equity-level owner-earnings model retains interest expense, the higher recurring coupon reduces projected owner earnings rather than the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 17, 2025, Mattel issued $ 600.0 million aggregate principal amount of 5.000 % 2025 Senior Notes due November 2030 (the "2025 Notes").
audit_findings.explanation: The timing error is demonstrated: the 5.000% notes replaced 3.375% notes only on November 17, 2025, so FY2025 contains little of the annual increase. The computed coupon difference is $9.75 million annually. Even treating that pre-tax amount conservatively as a dollar-for-dollar owner-earnings reduction lowers base value only to approximately $16.44 per share, still above the $14.53 price and leaving the scenario conclusion unchanged; the actual after-tax effect should be smaller.
audit_findings.action: Annualize interest expense from the post-refinancing debt schedule, include issuance-cost amortization and the tax effect in projected owner earnings, and confirm the resulting sensitivity without deducting debt principal again.
